1

--- Page 294 ---
possession was taken by the Mandal Revenue
Officer and that area may be symbolically
returned to him. If and when he approaches
such court, the Special Court will hold an
enquiry and pass appropriate orders. He may
also pursue such remedies as may be open to
him in regard to physical possession, if he
is able to identify and make out title.”
4. Learned Senior counsel for the applicant submits
that pursuant to the aforesaid order, he had approached
the  Land  Grabbing  Court  but  nothing  has  happened
thereafter. His relatives had moved the High Court for
the State of Telangana at Hyderabad (briefly ‘the High
Court’ hereinafter) in Writ Petition Petition No.10990
of 2011 and Writ Petition No.36401 of 2024, wherein the
following order was passed on 09.12.2025:
“21 In view of the principle laid down by the
Hon'ble Supreme Court in the above case,
without going into that aspect i.e. value of
the land, in order to put a quietus to the
litigation, this court deems it appropriate
to  direct  the  respondents  to  identify
appropriate land with mutual consent, without
any encumbrances in lieu of extent of the
land belonging to the petitioners in view of
the rights accrued on the petitioners and to
ensure the right guaranteed under Article
300-A  of  the  Constitution  of  India  and
accordingly  take  necessary  steps  in
accordance with law for allocating the same
to the petitioners and complete the entire
exercise  as  expeditiously  as  possible,
2

--- Page 295 ---
preferably, within a period of six months
from the date of receipt of a copy of this
order. In the absence of which, petitioners
are entitled to the just compensation to be
determined in terms of the Right to Fair
Compensation  and  Transparency  in  Land
Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement
Act, 2013, also known as the Land Acquisition
Act, 2013 and accordingly the respondents
shall take appropriate steps, in accordance
with law.”
5. In view thereof, we grant liberty to the applicant
to move the High Court for appropriate relief.

     IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION 
CRIMINAL APPEAL   No   4849 OF 2026  
(Arising out of SLP(Crl.) No.14014 of 2026)
ANITA PANDEY                   … APPELLANT
Versus
STATE OF UP & ANR.            … RESPONDENTS
O  R  D  E  R
1. Leave granted.
2. We have heard learned Senior Counsel for the parties and
perused the material placed on record with their able assistance.
3. It seems to us that the Complaint Case No. 344 of 2015,
arising out of Case Crime No. 489 of 2013 (Anita vs. Satyendra Nath
Shukla and others), instituted by the Appellant, was a counterblast
to the case, being Sessions Trial No. 2707 of 2014, instituted by
Respondent No. 2 herein. In our considered opinion, in view of the
principle laid down by this Court in Nathi Lal & Ors.  v. State of
U.P. & Anr. , 1990(Supp) SCC 145 , it would be in the interest of
justice  to  get  both  the  matters  tried  together.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO.           OF 2026
(@ SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CRIMINAL) NO.15535/2026)
DHEER SINGH PARMAR      APPELLANT(S)
VERSUS
STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH     RESPONDENT(S)
ORDER
1. Leave granted.
2. We have heard learned counsel for the appellant and
learned  counsel  for  the  respondent-State  of  Madhya
Pradesh.
3. Appellant is aggrieved by order dated 09.07.2026
passed by the High Court of Madhya Pradesh at Jabalpur
(briefly the ‘High Court’ hereinafter), rejecting the
regular bail application of the appellant.
4. Appellant  is  an  accused  in  Crime  No.418/2025
registered  at  Police  Station-  Naugon,  District-
Chhatarpur, Madhya Pradesh under Sections 8/20B, 27A and
29 of the Narcotics Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act,
1985 (for short, the ‘NDPS Act’).
5. Prosecution  case  is  that  based  on  confidential
information, a vehicle was intercepted from where 25
packets  of  ganja  were  recovered.  According  to  the
1

--- Page 306 ---
prosecution, appellant was driving the vehicle. Based on
his statement, another 182 packets were recovered from a
room, totalling 207 packets weighing 216.43 kgs.
6. Appellant was arrested on 25.06.2025 and has been in
custody since then.
7. This  Court  had  issued  notice  vide  order  dated
24.08.2026, pursuant to which the respondent-State of
Madhya Pradesh has filed counter affidavit.
8. Learned  counsel  for  the  appellant  submits  that
appellant  was  taken  into  custody  one  day  prior  to
25.06.2025 during midnight; not as per the prosecution
story. According to him, this is a make-believe narrative
built up by the police to implicate the appellant, who has
got no criminal history. He submits that if the CCTV
footage of the previous toll booth is examined, it would
establish the contention of the appellant that the vehicle
was not being driven through the toll gate on that fateful
evening.  In  addition  thereto,  there  are  serious
irregularities relating to interception of the vehicle and
seizure of the contraband.
9. On the contrary, learned counsel for the respondent-
State of Madhya Pradesh submits that the contraband seized
is much more than the commercial quantity. Contentions
raised by the appellant can only be gone and decided only
in the course of the trial. However, he fairly submits
that appellant has no criminal antecedent. Insofar the
trial is concerned, he submits that prosecution has cited
2

--- Page 307 ---
16 witnesses out of which, evidence of 06 witnesses have
been recorded thus far.
10. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and on
due consideration, we feel that appellant has suffered
detention for about a year and three months. The trial
does not appear to be nearing completion and will take its
own time. In such circumstances, we are of the considered
opinion that a case for bail is made out.
11. That being the position, t he impugned order dated
09.07.2026 passed by the High Court is set aside.
12. Consequently, we direct that the appellant shall be
produced before the jurisdictional Special Court within a
maximum period of 07 days from today, whereafter he shall
be released on bail on such terms and conditions as may be
deemed appropriate.
13. Accordingly, the Criminal Appeal is allowed.
14. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.

ARSH SAUDAGAR      APPELLANT(S)

THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH     RESPONDENT(S)
ORDER
1. Leave granted.
2. We have heard learned counsel for the appellant and
learned  counsel  for  the  respondent-State  of  Madhya
Pradesh.
3. Appellant is aggrieved by order dated 08.08.2025
passed by the High Court of Madhya Pradesh at Jabalpur
(briefly the ‘High Court’ hereinafter), rejecting the
regular bail application of the appellant.
4. Appellant  is  an  accused  in  Crime  No.406/2024
registered  at  Police  Station-  Kotwali,  District-
Chhatarpur, Madhya Pradesh under Sections 309(4), 317(2)
and 317(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (for
short, ‘BNS’) and Sections 25/27 of the Arms Act, 1959.
5. Allegation against the appellant is that he along
with other co-accused had looted the complainant after
1

--- Page 314 ---
intercepting his vehicle. From the vehicle, it was stated
with Rs.8,00,000/- in cash were robbed (subsequently the
amount was enhanced to Rs.20,00,000/-).
6. Appellant was arrested on 22.08.2024 and has been in
custody since then.
7. This  Court  had  issued  notice  vide  order  dated
06.07.2026, pursuant to which the respondent-State of
Madhya Pradesh has filed counter affidavit.
8. On 02.09.2026, we had called upon the learned counsel
for the respondent-State of Madhya Pradesh to place on
record the evidence of the 04 prosecution witnesses who
were examined till that point of time. The same has been
placed on record which we have perused.
9. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that during
the interregnum, one more co-accused has been granted
bail. Now a total of 06 co-accused have been granted bail
by the Trial Court and the High Court. Appellant is in
custody  for  more  than  two  years  now.  In  such
circumstances, appellant may be released on bail.
10. Learned counsel for the respondent-State of Madhya
Pradesh submits that the co-accused, who has been recently
granted  bail,  could  not  be  identified  in  the  Test
Identification  Parade  (TIP),  whereas  P.W.1  has
specifically named the appellant.
11. On a query by the Court, he fairly submits that out
of 22 prosecution witnesses cited by the prosecution, only
04 have been examined till date.
2

--- Page 315 ---
12. Be that as it may, having regard to the nature of the
allegations made against the appellant and the fact that
he has been in custody for more than two years now, we are
of the view that a case for bail is made out.
13. That being the position, t he impugned order dated
08.08.2025 passed by the High Court is set aside.
14. Consequently, we direct that the appellant shall be
produced before the Trial Court within a maximum period of
07 days from today, whereafter he shall be released on
bail on such terms and conditions as may be deemed
appropriate.
15. Accordingly, the Criminal Appeal is allowed.
16. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.

1

--- Page 342 ---
DIARY NO.51912/2026
                   
                           O R D E R
Permission to file the Special Leave Petition is
granted. 
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties. 
3. The  present  petition  has  been  filed  seeking
cancellation of bail granted to the respondent no.2 by the
High Court of Punjab and Haryana vide impugned order dated
12.08.2026 passed in CRM-M-19339-2026.
4. The allegation against the respondent no.2 is that he
was the master mind in the killing of two persons which
was executed by his two sons among others.
5. Learned  counsel  for  the  petitioner-complainant
submitted that the High Court without appreciating the
facts  and  circumstances  of  the  case  in  their  true
perspective, has allowed the prayer for bail, when the
respondent no.2 had been in custody only for about a year
and two months. It was contended that the FIR itself
narrates that the entire incident occurred at the behest
of the respondent no.2 and when the attack happened, an
attempt was made to contact him to control his sons, who
had came at the scene of occurrence, but at that time also
on phone he reiterated the threat that they will kill the
family  members  of  the  petitioner.  Learned  Counsel
2

--- Page 343 ---
DIARY NO.51912/2026
submitted that the prayer for bail of co-accused, namely,
Neeraj Kumar, son of the respondent no.2 has been refused
by this Court. 
6. Learned  counsel  for  the  respondent  no.1-State  of
Punjab submits that there is allegation of the respondent
no.2 being the master mind. However, the fact that he has
not been assigned any overt role in the incident, is not
denied. Further, it has been submitted that out of 32
chargesheet witnesses, 05 have been examined and 02 have
been given up and the next date fixed is 8th of this month.
7. Learned counsel for the respondent no.2 submits that
the respondent no.2 has no criminal record and is aged
about 70 years having medical issues. It was submitted
that to rope in the entire family, he has been added as an
accused in the FIR. It was his contention that even if the
allegations are taken to be true, the respondent no.2
admittedly not being at the spot, no vicarious liability
can be fastened on him just because of his relationship
with two of the named accused. It was further submitted
that there is no allegation of any misuse of the privilege
of bail or the respondent no.2 not cooperating in the
trial.  Learned  counsel  submitted  that  the  refusal  to
enlarge the co-accused Neeraj Kumar on bail was primarily
because  of  his  criminal  antecedents  and  he  was  also
physically present at the spot, as alleged in the FIR.
3

--- Page 344 ---
DIARY NO.51912/2026
8. Having considered the matter in its entirety, and
primarily for the reason that the respondent no.2 is aged
70 years, in the peculiar facts and circumstances and the
condition of the respondent no.2, without going into the
merits of the case, we are not persuaded to interfere in
the order impugned.
9. However, the State/prosecution is directed to ensure
that the witnesses are produced in the trial on the dates
fixed without any delay. The Trial Court is also directed
to ensure that the trial proceeds at a good pace without
fixing long dates in the matter.
10. It goes without saying that the respondent no.2 shall
fully cooperate during the trial.
11.  We further clarify that the benefit of the present
order will not be available to other co-accused.
12. The Special Leave Petition stands disposed of in the
aforementioned terms.
13. Pending  application(s),  if  any,  shall  also  stand
disposed of.

continued cooperation of the appellant before the

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
We  have  heard  the  learned  Senior  Counsel
appearing for the petitioners, the learned Solicitor
General appearing for the respondent-State and Mr.
K. Parmeshwar, learned Senior Counsel appearing for
the private respondent(s).
Against the refusal of the interim order sought
for by the petitioners before the High Court, the
present Special Leave Petition has been filed.
Learned  Senior  Counsel  appearing  for  the
petitioners would contend that the order passed by
the High Court requires interference, as it has
wrongly taken into consideration the earlier order
passed, which pertains to a different set of bank
accounts. It is his further submission that in the
present  proceedings,  the  petitioners  seek
appropriate orders for their expenses other than the
ones for their day to day administration, including
election expenses.
Learned Solicitor General, appearing for the
respondent-State, would submit that the present case
involves a new set of allegations which is inclusive
of huge  deposit having been  made and the alleged
involvement of the Government land(s), being sold
after its illegal transfer.

--- Page 359 ---
3
Mr.  K.  Parmeshwar,  learned  Senior  counsel
appearing  for  the  private  respondent(s),  would
submit  that  vide  order  dated  17.09.2026,  the
Election Commission has frozen the symbol of the
petitioner(s) and, therefore, the larger issue that
has to be decided is as to who is actually entitled
for the amount in the bank accounts. Releasing any
amount  in  favour  of  the  petitioners,  without
adjudication, would cause substantial prejudice to
the other party in the  lis before the Election
Commission.
We are of the considered view that expressing
anything on the merits of this case will have a
substantial bearing on the writ petition pending
before the High Court. The arguments made before us
are meant to be taken up and decided in the main
matter by the High Court.
Keeping that in mind, we refrain from going
into the merits, particularly, when we are dealing
with an interim order passed in a pending writ
petition.
Accordingly, we are not inclined to exercise
our  jurisdiction  under  Article  136  of  the
Constitution of India, 1950, except for requesting
the High Court to expedite the hearing in the
pending writ petition.

--- Page 360 ---
4
The Special Leave Petition stands disposed of,
accordingly.
Pending  application(s),  if  any,  shall  also
stand disposed of.

Leave granted.
The appellant has been convicted for the
offences punishable under Sections 302, 379 read
with Section 201 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860
and was sentenced to undergo imprisonment for
1

--- Page 373 ---
life, along with fine and default stipulations.
The judgment of conviction and order on sentence
rendered by the Trial Court, has been confirmed by
the High Court,  vide the impugned order dated
11.04.2023. Aggrieved by the same, the appellant
is before this Court. 
Learned counsel appearing for the appellant
submits  that  it  is  a  case  of  circumstantial
evidence and the occurrence is of the year 2013.
It is the further say of the learned counsel for
the appellant that there are arguable issue in
the present appeal.
Learned counsel appearing for the respondent
submits that both the Courts have concurrently
held against the appellant. There is no need for
granting suspension of sentence.
Considering the submissions, we are inclined
to grant suspension of sentence by taking note of
the facts governing, particularly, when it is a
case of circumstantial evidence which requires to
be gone into at the time of finally disposing of
the matter.
Accordingly, the sentence imposed upon
the appellant stands suspended, and he is granted
2

--- Page 374 ---

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Leave granted.

--- Page 382 ---
2
2. Brihanmumbai  Municipal  Corporation  (BMC)  is  before  us
challenging the impugned judgment of the High Court, which reversed
the order of the Bombay City Civil Court. On brief facts, the BMC
issued a notice for removal of unauthorized structure, which was
encroaching a road. The 1 st respondent filed a suit challenging the
notice before the Bombay City Civil Court, which was dismissed,
which stood reversed by the High Court. The High Court allowed
reliefs A and B prayed in the suit, finding the notice issued to be
bad in law and restraining the defendants from enforcing the
impugned notice or demolishing or removing the shop in the suit
premises.
3. Sri Siddarth Bhatnagar, learned Senior Counsel appearing for
the appellant, by I.A. No.295241 of 2026 points out that the
structure of the 1 st respondent obstructs the passage of the main
road and it is expedient that the same may be removed. It is his
contention that the BMC has three alternate spaces of the same
extent, one of which can be allotted to the 1 st respondent subject
to the final disposal of the appeal.
4. Sri Gaurav Agarwal, learned Senior Counsel for the respondents
on the other hand submits that the building cannot be said to be on
the middle of the road and the 1st respondent has been carrying on a
‘Rent a Car’, which is the only livelihood of the 1st respondent. It
is also claimed that the said building was in possession of the 1 st
respondent  as  permitted  by  the  Maharashtra  Housing  and  Area
Development Authority for long.
5. As of now, we are only concerned with the interim direction to
be issued. We have seen photographs produced by the appellant
herein and the 1 st respondent. The fact remains that though the
structure which is said to be in the possession of 1st respondent is
not in the middle of the road, it definitely obstructs and
restricts the passage of the widened road. In the circumstances, to
adjust equities, we are of the opinion that the appellant/BMC
should be permitted to immediately demolish the structure. The 1 st
respondent shall hand over vacant possession of the building within
two weeks from today. If the same is not done, the BMC would be

--- Page 383 ---
3
entitled to take vacant possession after taking an inventory of any
moveables found in the structure. BMC shall also be permitted to
demolish the structure. However, subject to the final disposal of
this appeal, the three options suggested by the BMC shall be
offered to the 1 st respondent and she shall be entitled to choose
one of them. We make it clear that the 1 st respondent’s entitlement
will be decided in this appeal, and the entitlement to continue
occupying the alternate accommodation would be subject to that.
6. Let the records be called for. Respondent No.2 to file counter
affidavit, if any.
7. List the matter on 02.12.2026.
 (VISHAL ANAND)                                    (POOJA SHARMA)
DEPUTY REGISTRAR                                 COURT MASTER (NSH)

Petition(s) for Special Leave to Appeal (C)  No(s).  27440/2024
[Arising out of impugned final judgment and order dated  23-04-2024
in WA No. 395/2024 passed by the High Court of Madhya Pradesh
Principal Seat at Jabalpur]
SITARAM SEN                                        Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
GENERAL MANGER                                     Respondent(s)
IA No. 253369/2024 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING O.T.
 
Date : 12-10-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM :  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SATISH CHANDRA SHARMA
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE NONGMEIKAPAM KOTISWAR SINGH
For Petitioner(s) :Mr. Vardhman Kaushik, AOR
                   Mr. Nitin, Adv.
                   
                   
For Respondent(s) :Mr. Brijender Chahar, A.S.G.
                   Mr. Digvijay Dam, Adv.
                   Mr. Prashant Singh-ii, Adv.
                   Ms. Mili Baxi, Adv.
                   Ms. Prerna Dhal, Adv.
                   Ms. Sweksha, Adv.
                   Mr. Shreekant Neelappa Terdal- 909, AOR
                   
                   
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The petitioner has preferred this petition against
the order dated 23.04.2024 passed by the High Court of
Madhya Pradesh at Jabalpur, dismissing Writ Appeal No. 395
of 2024.
1

--- Page 406 ---
2. The facts of the case reveal that an advertisement
was  issued  by  Ordnance  Factory,  Katni,  inviting
applications for the post of Barber on 16.01.1998. The
petitioner,  having  qualified  for  the  said  post,  was
appointed  as  a  daily-wage  Barber.  His  services  were
continued from time to time, and he served for nearly six
years until his engagement was brought to an end.
3. Aggrieved  thereby,  the  petitioner  preferred  an
Original  Application  before  the  Central  Administrative
Tribunal (O.A. No. 460 of 2007), which was disposed of with
a direction to the respondents therein to consider his
representation. The petitioner was ultimately terminated on
29.09.2007.
4. Thereafter, the petitioner approached the Industrial
Tribunal.  The  Industrial  Tribunal,  vide  award  dated
13.01.2015, held the termination to be in violation of
Section 25F of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, and
awarded compensation of Rs. 1,50,000/-.
5. The  Writ  Petition  as  well  as  the  Writ  Appeal
preferred by the petitioner before the High Court of Madhya
Pradesh against the said ward were dismissed.
6. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits
that once the termination was held to be bad in law for
non-compliance with Section 25F of the Industrial Disputes
Act, 1947, the petitioner ought to have been reinstated in
service, and in any event, the compensation awarded was
2

--- Page 407 ---
exceedingly meager.
7. Learned counsel appearing for the respondent-Union
of India has vehemently opposed the prayer, contending that
the compensation awarded by the Tribunal in the year 2015
was just and reasonable in the facts and circumstances of
the case.
8. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and
taking  into  account  the  totality  of  facts  and
circumstances, this Court is of the opinion that the
compensation awarded in the matter deserves to be enhanced.
The compensation is accordingly enhanced to Rs. 5,00,000/-
which shall be paid to the petitioner within a period of
six weeks from today.
9. With the aforesaid observations, the Special Leave
Petition stands disposed of.
10. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of. 
  (RAHUL KUMAR)                                    (KOMAL)
COURT MASTER (SH)                             COURT MASTER (NSH)
3

CORAM :  HON'BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE JOYMALYA BAGCHI

                   Mr. Anurag Tiwary, Adv.
Ms. T. Geetha, Adv.
                                      
For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. An incident involving a sit-in protest by certain lawyers,
including the petitioners, took place on the intervening night of
20/21.08.2026 within the premises of the Bar Council of India. The
protest was stated to have escalated in the early hours of
21.08.2026 when, at about 1:15 a.m., a group of approximately 20 to
30 persons arrived at the premises and violently assaulted the
petitioners who were participating in the protest.
1

--- Page 418 ---
2. This led the petitioners to file a complaint on 22.08.2026,
before SHO, IP Estate Police Station, New Delhi, for offences of
unlawful  assembly,  rioting,  grievous  hurt,  trespass,  criminal
intimidation and conspiracy. They also sought preservation of CCTV
footage.  However, it is their case that no FIR was registered on
the basis of the aforesaid complaint.
3. The petitioners then filed a Writ Petition before this court,
but upon mentioning, they were advised to approach the Delhi High
Court.  Vide impugned judgment dated 21.09.2026, the High Court has
dismissed the Writ Petition as being non-maintainable, primarily on
the ground that the petitioners have an alternate efficacious
remedy in the form of filing a complaint before the concerned
Magistrate under Section 223 BNSS.
4. We have heard learned counsel for the petitioners and perused
the averments in the complaint made to the Police on 22.08.2026.
5. We are conscious of the fact that no notice has been issued to
the respondents and we do not propose to pass an order that may be
construed to have caused any prejudice to them. However, to ensure
that the incident is properly investigated and such investigation
is taken to a logical conclusion, we dispose of the instant Special
Leave Petition with the following directions:
(i) The Commissioner of Police, Delhi, is directed to ensure that
the complaint dated 22.08.2026 made by the petitioners to the SHO,
IP Estate Police Station is appropriately investigated. For that
purpose, let a Special Investigation Team (SIT) headed by a senior
police officer in the rank of Deputy Commissioner of Police be
constituted.
2

--- Page 419 ---
(ii) The investigation shall be conducted uninfluenced by the
observations made by the High Court in the impugned order.
(iii) The report upon investigation may be filed before the
jurisdictional Metropolitan Magistrate with an intimation to the
petitioners.
(iv)   The petitioners shall be at liberty to approach the High
Court, if so required.
6. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand closed.
(NITIN TALREJA)                            (PREETHI DILEEP KUMAR)

High Court’ hereinafter).
1

--- Page 424 ---

Customs,  (Airport  and  Air  Cargo),  Kolkata  has
preferred statutory appeal(s) before the High Court
being CUSTA No.21 of 2025 and CUSTA No.22 of 2025,
assailing the orders passed by the Customs, Excise &
Service Tax Appellate Tribunal (for short, ‘CESTAT’),
Eastern Zonal Bench, Kolkata.
6. It appears that the petitioner(s) through their
lawyers had appeared before the High Court to resist
admission of the appeals by raising the plea of
maintainability. However, the High Court, vide the
impugned  order  dated  10.07.2026,  rejected  the
preliminary prayer of the respondent(s) for hearing
maintainability of the appeal(s) at the admission
stage  and  directed  the  respondents  (petitioners
herein) to withdraw from the Bar, whereafter it was
directed  that  the  appeals  of  the  appellant
(respondent herein) would be heard  ex-parte on the
question of admission and on the prayers for  ad
interim relief.
7. Petitioner-in-person submits that much prior to
the  date  fixed  for  admission  hearing,  i.e.  on
21.07.2026, the appeals were already admitted on
17.02.2026 but no interim relief was granted.
8. If this be the position, we are of the view that
the  respondents  (petitioners  herein)  should  be
allowed to participate in the appeal proceedings and
2

--- Page 425 ---
raise all legally permissible contentions before the
High  Court,  including  on  the  issue  of
maintainability. We are further of the view that the

notwithstanding admission of the appeals.

disposed of.

disposed of.

1. The petitioner has been convicted under Sections 20(b)

Substances Act, 1985 (for short “the NDPS Act”), and was
sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of
twelve  years  and  was  imposed  a  fine  of  Rs.1,00,000/-
(Rupees One Lakh Only) by the Trial Court in connection with
NCB Case No.03/NCB/Ranchi/2022 registered at Police Station
NCB Ranchi, Jharkhand. The Petitioner has preferred an
appeal against the order of conviction before the High
Court;  citing  irregularities  in  the  sampling  of  the
contraband,   absence of independent witnesses etc. The
appeal is pending before the High Court.
2. The petitioner, aged 28 was the driver of a truck which
was intercepted by the NCB Team, along with the co-accused
helper. From the truck, 204 Kgs of Ganja was recovered
during search. The petitioner has been in judicial custody
for over four years and four months since 19.05.2022.
3. The learned Counsel for the Petitioner submitted that
the  Petitioner  was  merely  a  truck  driver  and  had  no
SLP(Crl.) No.18769/2026                                                            2

--- Page 452 ---
ownership over the truck, and that he had no conscious
possession of the contraband. It was further submitted that
this  court  had  earlier  suspended  the  sentence  of  the

the Petitioner when the truck was intercepted. It is also
submitted  that  on  investigation,  the  person  who  was
responsible  for  the  transportation  of  ganja  was  also
identified and arraigned in the case, and that he has also
been granted bail.

of the petitioner.

conditions as the trial court may deem fit to impose, till

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CIVIL APPEAL NO. 637/2016
HIMACHAL PRADESH HOUSING URBAN 
DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY & ANR. Appellant(s)
                                VERSUS
SHRI DEEP CHAND                                    Respondent(s)
WITH 
C.A. No. 639/2016
C.A. No. 638/2016
C.A. No. 3972/2016
C.A. No. 3369/2016
C.A. No. 3973/2016
C.A. No. 6083/2016
C.A. No. 6974/2016
O R D E R
1. The  present  appeals  are  arising  out  of  order  dated
17.04.2015 passed in CWP No. 1606/2015.
2. The facts of the case reveals that the respondent was
engaged as a Beldar on daily wage basis in the month of July,
1991. He was assigned the job of mustrol of Work Inspector in
the month of September, 1992 and he has completed 10 years of
continuous service with 240 days in each calender year in the
year 2002. However, he was conferred with the status of work
charge employee only w.e.f. 17.07.2007.
3. The respondent’s grievance before the courts below was
that he is entitled to be conferred with the work charge status

--- Page 469 ---
2
w.e.f. 01.01.2003 instead of 17.07.2007 and is entitled for
arrears of financial benefits on actual basis for the preceding
three years. It was also contented before the High Court that
similarly placed employees have been granted the same benefit
to be more specific Deepak Kumar and Dheeraj Sharma by virtue
of judgment passed in LPA No. 491/2011 on 15.05.2012. The
Division Bench of the High Court while allowing the writ
petition granted the similar benefit to the respondent herein
on the analogy of Deepak Kumar and Dheeraj Sharma by observing
that the respondent had been considered differently by the
appellant herein. 
4. We do not find any reason to interfere with the well
reasoned order passed by the High Court. In the peculiar facts
and circumstances of the case, the Civil Appeals are dismissed.
5. Pending applications, if any, shall stand disposed of.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CIVIL APPEAL NO. 565/2016
NADIAD MUNCIPALITY CORORATION                 Appellant(s)
                                VERSUS
THE STATE OF GUJARAT & ORS.                        Respondent(s)
O R D E R
1. The appellant Nadiad Municipality Corporation before this
Court is aggrieved by the order dated 17.10.2011 passed by the
High Court of Gujarat at Ahmedabad in Letters Patent Appeal
(LPA)  No.  1145/2002  by  which  the  LPA  preferred  by  the
Municipality Corporation was dismissed. The facts of the case
reveal that the respondents raised a dispute claiming permanent
status and continuity in service w.e.f. 01.01.2000 and the
Industrial Tribunal in reference I.T No. 141/1998 passed an
award on 28.08.2001, partly accepting the claim of 21 workmen
and they were directed to be made permanent w.e.f. 01.01.2000
and as well as the benefit of continuity in service was
granted.
2. It is an undisputed fact that the claim made by the
respondent Union/workmen remain unchallenged meaning thereby
the Municipality Corporation did not examine any witnesses nor
did it produce any evidence before the Tribunal and in absence
of any effective defense an award was passed on 28.08.2001.

--- Page 472 ---
2
3. The award was challenged before the High Court of Gujarat
and the learned Single Judge vide order dated 26.03.2002 passed
in Special Civil Application No. 3499/2012 has dismissed the
Writ Petition summarily against which the LPA was preferred and
the Division Bench of the High Court of Gujarat has dismissed
the LPA also.
4. It is pertinent to note that the Review Petition was also
preferred in the matter and it was also dismissed vide order
dated 04.10.2013.
5. This court does not find any reason to interfere with
finding of facts arrived at by the Industrial Tribunal vide
order dated 28.08.2001 and also does not find any reason to
interfere with the order passed by the High Court.
6. Accordingly, the Civil Appeal is dismissed.
7. The workers shall be entitled for all consequential benefits
as awarded by the Industrial Tribunal.
8. Pending applications, if any, shall stand disposed of.

O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. The Division Bench of the High Court of Judicature at Bombay 1 vide
the impugned order dated 04 th March, 2026 has disposed of an interim
application2 in an appeal 3 carried by the insurer-respondent no.1 under
Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, from an award of the relevant
Motor  Accidents  Claims  T ribunal,  by  making  certain  directions  without
even issuing notice to the claimants/appellants, who are the respondents
in such appeal.
3. Disposal of an interim application without notice to the opponent is
something which is rather unusual. The High Court has proceeded in clear
breach of principles of natural justice; hence, the impugned order insofar
as  it  records  disposal  of  the  interim  application  stands  set  aside.
Consequently, the interim application shall stand revived on the file of the
High Court. We request the roster Bench of the High Court to rehear the
1 High Court
2 I.A. No.1671 of 2026
3 First Appeal No.194 of 2026

--- Page 475 ---
2
interim application in the presence of the claimants/appellants. 
4. Having regard to the age of the first appellant 4 (he is 87 years old)
who has lost his son in the fatal road accident, we request the roster
Bench of the High Court to decide the interim application in terms of this
order  as  expeditiously  as  possible,  and  preferably  by  the  end  of
December, 2026.
5. We record that a sum of Rs.5 crore in terms of the impugned order
has  been made  over  to  the  claimants/appellants.  Whether  or  not  the
insurer-respondent no.1 should be made liable to pay any further sum to
the claimants/appellants out of the sum awarded may be decided by the
High  Court  in  accordance  with  law.  All  contentions  and  objections  on
merits are left open. 
6. The civil appeal is, accordingly, disposed of.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
IA No.198894/2026
1. Heard the learned counsels appearing for the parties.
2. Petitioner/applicant  has  been  arraigned  as  an  accused  for  the  offences
punishable under Section 307 read with Section 34 of the  Indian Penal Code,
1860 (IPC) later converted into Section 302 IPC, came  to be convicted after trial
by judgment dated 07.09.1990.
1

--- Page 502 ---
3. On an appeal being filed by all the accused persons, Uday Nath Pandey, (co-
accused), came to be acquitted for the offences under Section 302 IPC. The
present  petitioner/applicant  and  co-accused,  Kundan  Pandey,  came  to  be
convicted and one more co-accused by name Smt. Kusum Devi died during the
pendency of the appeal before the High Court and as such appeal got abated. 
4. Having heard the learned counsels appearing for the parties, we notice that
the cause for death as evidenced from the post-morten report is due to shock
and haemorrhage on account of the injuries sustained. The injury sustained by
the deceased is as under:
“Bruise 4" x 1/2" over lower part of the Rt side of chest laterally.
On dissection there was fracture of 8th & 9th ribs on the Rt side
of chest. There was laceration of the liver. There was fracture of
9th & 10th ribs on the left side of the chest. There was laceration
of the spleen. The abdominal cavity was full of blood.” 
5. Even according to the charge-sheet material the appellant was having a lathi
and he had assaulted the deceased twice. As to whether the fatal injuries are
attributable to the appellant or the injuries sustained due to the assault made
by Smt. Kusum Devi , is an issue which will have to be evaluated by this Court
on re-appreciation of the evidence since prima facie the medical evidence does
not corroborate the injury allegedly caused by lathi on the deceased.
6. Hence,  we  are  of  the  considered  view  that  petitioner/applicant  –  Rabin
Pandey alias Rabindra Pandey, is entitled for the grant of bail by suspending the
sentence imposed on him subject to the terms and conditions as jurisdictional
court may deem fit to impose.
7. Accordingly Interlocutory Application stands allowed.
2

--- Page 503 ---
Registry to verify filing of I A No.24646/2026 and list the same along with
the main matter(s).
List the matter(s) after six weeks.
(RASHI GUPTA)                                   (AVGV RAMU)

registered against him before the learned District and Additional

details of the past criminal cases registered against him is fatal

For Respondent(s) :  
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
IA No. 314272/2026
It appears from the records that the petitioner
was released on default bail on 19.09.2026 by the
trial court.
Meanwhile, the regular bail application which
was pending before the Calcutta High Court, came up
for hearing on 05.10.2026 when the High Court found
that since the chargesheet has been subsequently
1

--- Page 689 ---
filed after lapse of 90 days and the trial court has
granted default bail, the High Court found no case
for bail to be made out and, therefore, the order of
default bail dated 19.09.2026 was set aside by the
High Court.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that
due to lack of communication between the client and
the counsel for the petitioner, the counsel could
not inform the Calcutta High Court that the default
bail had already been granted when the order dated
05.10.2026 was passed by the Calcutta High Court
which is the subject matter of challenge in the
special leave petition.
Accordingly, for the aforesaid reasons and the
reasons contained in the application, the same is
allowed.
Consequently, the petitioner is exempted from
surrendering subject to furnishing bail bonds of
Rs.50,000/- within a period of 15 days and to the
satisfaction of the jurisdictional magistrate.
List before the regular bench as per Roster.
(VARSHA)                              (AJEET SINGH TARIYAL)
SR. PERSONAL ASTT.                      BRANCH OFFICER

ARVISH                                             Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
STATE OF RAJASTHAN & ORS.                          Respondent(s)
Seeking transfer of FIR No.002 of 2025 registered at Police Station
Ganj, District Ajmer, Rajasthan to Police Station Welcome, District
North East Delhi. 
 
Date : 12-10-2026 This petition was called on for hearing today.
CORAM : 
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ATUL S. CHANDURKAR
                           [IN CHAMBER]
For Petitioner(s) : Ms. Sugandha Anand- 3167 , AOR
                   
For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1.  Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner.
2.  The prayer made in the present Transfer Petition is for
transfer of FIR No.002/2025 that was originally registered at
Police Station Welcome, North East Delhi but was subsequently
transferred to Police Station Ganj, District Ajmer, Rajasthan only
to be again transferred to Police Station Welcome, North East
Delhi.
3.  In view of the decisions of this Court in Dr. Ram Chander
Singh Sagar and Another Vs. State of Tamil Nadu and Another  1   and
Rhea Chakraborty  Vs.  State of Bihar and others  2  , exercise of
jurisdiction under Section 406 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1  1978 INSC 12
2  2020 INSC 500

--- Page 743 ---
1973 is not permissible for transfer of investigation. 
4. Even otherwise, I do not find that there is any exceptional
case made out to invoke jurisdiction under Article 142 of the
Constitution of India to order such transfer.  
5. In that view of the matter, the prayer made in the Transfer
Petition cannot be granted. The Transfer Petition is therefore
dismissed.
6. It is, however, open for the petitioner to seek redressal of
her grievances in this regard, in accordance with law.
Pending Interlocutory Application(s), if any, shall stand
disposed of.
(NEETU SACHDEVA)                                (MANOJ KUMAR)
DEPUTY REGISTRAR                               COURT MASTER (NSH)
